Thread pool starvation does not hang the application, it makes it slow, and it makes it slow in a way that no profiler flags: the CPU is idle, no query is slow, and every individual operation looks fine. What is wrong is that the pool has no thread left to run the next work item, because the previous ones are all blocked waiting for something. The AI for .NET Developers hub brings together practical AI topics, learning paths, and selected .NET AI SDK and framework releases. Community Pulse combines technical links and insights from selected .NET accounts on Bluesky and Mastodon with linked discussions from r/dotnet over the last seven days. You can search all posts or filter by platform. The Reddit pilot adds up to four links per day; its authors are not selected Community Pulse accounts.
You can filter by topic and content type, bookmark stories, hide sources, track read items, and choose a compact layout. These preferences are stored locally in your browser; no account is required.
The AI hub starts with AI applied to .NET; broader AI coverage is available through its Coverage filter. Videos offer language, duration, and format filters. Language labels marked “estimated” come from titles and descriptions; audio metadata is used when available. Formats are inferred from descriptions and duration, so some videos remain unspecified.
Story topics are assigned from their titles and excerpts, independently of a source's specialties. Excerpts use publisher wording with boilerplate removed; reading times use a publisher-provided value when available, otherwise an estimate from supplied article text. Corrections can be submitted through a GitHub issue.
To suggest an RSS feed, YouTube channel, or community account, see Contribute. For issues or questions, reach out on GitHub or LinkedIn.

Have a .NET-related blog or YouTube channel to suggest? Contributions from creators and readers are welcome. Sources should regularly publish content relevant to .NET developers; related cloud, DevOps, and AI content is welcome when it is useful to that audience.
Suggest an RSS feed or YouTube channel The easiest way is to open a source suggestion with the feed or channel URL and a short explanation of its relevance. No repository changes are required.
If you prefer to contribute a pull request:
Check the existing Sources to avoid duplicates. Add one .yml file for the source in the repository's data/ folder, using the existing files as examples. Include Feed (the public RSS URL or YouTube channel URL), Title (the source name), and Website (the source's website URL). Add a short Description and a Topics list describing its usual specialties; Author is optional. Specialties describe the source and do not determine each story's tags. Open a pull request with a brief explanation of the source's relevance to .NET developers. For example:
1Feed: https://www.mytechramblings.com/index.xml 2Title: My technical ramblings 3Website: https://www.mytechramblings.com/ 4Description: Technical ramblings from a software engineer 5Topics: [.NET, Azure, AWS] 6Author: Carlos Pons To propose an account for Community Pulse, open a GitHub issue with its Bluesky or Mastodon profile and why its posts would be relevant. Community accounts are curated separately from the data/ feed files; do not add them there.
Suggestions are reviewed for fit and reliability. Submission does not guarantee inclusion or publication of every post.
Report a content correction Open an issue with the original story URL and the incorrect excerpt, topic, language, or video format. Include your proposed correction so it can be reviewed.
